questions.question: What does computational geometry primarily study?
options: B) Algorithms and data structures for geometric problems
questions.explanation: Geometry supplies the objects; algorithm design and analysis supply methods and guarantees.

source.file: 00) COT4521, 5520 slides - what is computational geometry.pdf

questions.question: Which question belongs to computability?
options: A) How many bytes does an implementation use?
B) How does time grow with n?
C) Does an algorithm exist for this problem?
D) Which valid algorithm is fastest?
questions.explanation: Computability concerns existence; complexity concerns resources.

questions.question: In the course Real RAM model, what is the cost of one primitive array read?
options: C) It depends on the numeric value stored
questions.explanation: An individual array read is an atomic operation in this model.

questions.question: What defines worst-case time for input size n?
options: A) Average time over unspecified inputs
B) Maximum executed instruction count among inputs of size n
C) Minimum time among all inputs
D) Largest coordinate in the input
questions.explanation: Worst-case analysis maximizes over inputs of a fixed size.

questions.question: Which statement expresses a tight asymptotic bound?
options: D) f equals g at one input
questions.explanation: Theta requires both an upper and lower asymptotic bound.

questions.question: Does f(n) = O(n²) prove that f grows quadratically?
options: A) No; O means a lower bound
B) No; linear functions also satisfy that upper bound
C) Yes; all upper bounds are tight
D) Yes; O always means exact growth
questions.explanation: Big O permits loose upper bounds; use Theta for a tight classification.

questions.question: Which order is from slower to faster asymptotic growth?
options: A) log n, n, n log n, n²
B) n, log n, n², n log n
C) n log n, log n, n, n²
D) n², n log n, n, log n
questions.explanation: The listed hierarchy compares sufficiently large inputs.

questions.question: What is the tight bound for 8n² + 3n + 100?
questions.explanation: The highest-degree term dominates and constants do not affect Theta.

questions.question: A full scan is followed by another full scan. What is the time?
Loops enumerate every unordered pair of distinct points. How many pairs are there?
questions.explanation: Choose two indices; avoid self-pairs and reverse duplicates.

questions.question: For n = 12, how many unordered distinct pairs are checked?
A loop doubles i from 1 while i < n. Its iteration count is what order?
questions.explanation: After t doublings i is 2^t, so reaching n takes logarithmically many steps.

questions.question: An outer n-step loop contains an independent log n-step loop. What is the total?
questions.explanation: The inner cost is paid n times.

questions.question: Changing from log base 2 to log base 10 changes what?
options: B) Logarithmic time to linear time
D) The input size to its square
questions.explanation: The change-of-base formula multiplies by a fixed constant.

questions.question: What is the solution to T(n) = 2T(n/2) + Θ(n), with constant-size base cases?
questions.explanation: There are logarithmically many levels with linear work at each level; this is an application exercise.

questions.question: An algorithm sorts in O(n log n) and scans in O(n). Its combined upper bound is what?
questions.explanation: Add sequential phases and keep the dominant term.

questions.question: Which claim about Ω notation is correct?
options: A) It is a lower bound on the function being analyzed
B) It always means best-case running time
C) It always means average-case time
questions.explanation: The case and the direction of a bound are separate concepts.

questions.question: Can a constant-size output require nonconstant computation?
options: A) Only if arithmetic is forbidden
B) No; output size always equals running time
C) Only when n is at most two
D) Yes; closest pair returns two points but must examine the input
questions.explanation: Input processing and output size are distinct costs; this applies the cost model to geometric problems.
